description: spring-data's classification against the conformance corpus (conformance/actions.json). 'adapterUnsupported' lists 'conformance' actions this adapter cannot express, each with the reason (naming the real mechanism) and the substring its thrown error must contain. 'adapterSupportedExpected' lists 'expectedUnsupported' actions this adapter deliberately translates, so they are oracle-compared instead of thrown. 'expectedUnsupportedMessages' pins the throw message for every 'expectedUnsupported' action it does not promote, and 'nullRepresentationOmittedMessages' for every 'nullRepresentationOmitted' action. validate-corpus.sh checks all four against the corpus; the harness refuses to run with a message missing.

The Criteria API has no cast expression: a predicate compares a path against a literal or another path. The reference's one string() form is over a BOOLEAN column, whose CEL text is exactly "true" or "false" and is compared in Java; over any other column type string() is refused in the leaf operand, because a number's text form is what the dialects render on their own terms and nothing in the Criteria API reproduces CEL's
adapterUnsupported.message: Unexpected string() expression in leaf operand of eq

adapterUnsupported.reason: The comparison is a_optional_string against a concatenation of a constant with the primary key. The reference lowers CEL's `+` as arithmetic, which requires numeric operands; CEL's string overload has no arithmetic meaning and is refused rather than rendered as a numeric addition
adapterUnsupported.message: Arithmetic comparison requires numeric operands, got String

adapterUnsupported.reason: The same arithmetic-only lowering of `+`, reached with both operands columns instead of one being a constant. The reference refuses every string `+`, so it needs no type information to reject the two-column form
adapterUnsupported.message: Arithmetic comparison requires numeric operands, got String

adapterUnsupported.reason: CEL carries a NaN or signed infinity through the arithmetic composed on top of a division, and SQL has no value that does — the NULLIF divide-by-zero guard turns the whole sum into NULL. The reference's non-finite rewrite only reaches a division that IS the comparison operand, so a division nested inside further arithmetic fails closed rather than emitting the under-granting filter
adapterUnsupported.message: arithmetic composed on a division whose denominator may be zero is not supported: CEL carries the resulting NaN or infinity through the surrounding arithmetic and SQL has no value that does

adapterUnsupported.reason: Same nested-division limitation as cr-div-then-add. This is the arm that proves it matters: `NaN != 2.0` is TRUE and the PDP allows the zero row, while `NULL + 1 <> 2` is UNKNOWN and drops it
adapterUnsupported.message: arithmetic composed on a division whose denominator may be zero is not supported: CEL carries the resulting NaN or infinity through the surrounding arithmetic and SQL has no value that does

adapterUnsupported.reason: CEL `%` is integer-only while attribute values are doubles, so a satisfiable policy has to cast with int() first — and int() has no faithful SQL lowering, CAST rounding where CEL truncates toward zero. The same limitation refuses cast-int-double
adapterUnsupported.message: mod is not supported in comparisons: CEL % is integer-only while attribute values are always doubles at check time, so a satisfiable policy must cast with int() first

adapterUnsupported.reason: Positional access into a list of numbers. The reference lowers a list attribute only as a JPA collection, a joined table whose rows carry no order a plan can name, so the leaf resolver has no index() form and refuses the operand before the list attribute is resolved. The element's type never comes into it, and neither does the mapping: the corpus maps aNumberList as a related table of element rows, which the membership actions (in-number-list, hasint-number-list-vs-string) read and this refusal never reaches
adapterUnsupported.message: Unexpected index() expression in leaf operand of eq

adapterUnsupported.reason: map() translates only as the collection operand of hasIntersection, where the projection becomes the inner select of an EXISTS. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list has no Criteria form
adapterUnsupported.message: Direct comparison of map(...) to a value is not supported (operator: eq). Wrap the map() expression in hasIntersection(map(...), [...]) instead.

adapterUnsupported.reason: Cerbos splits a path on an empty delimiter into one segment per character, so the relation is a strict string-prefix test; the reference lowers descendentOf as `LIKE prefix + delimiter + '%'`, which with an empty delimiter also matches the path itself (a2, never its own descendant). The empty delimiter is refused when the hierarchy operand is resolved, before that LIKE is built
adapterUnsupported.message: hierarchy delimiter must be a non-empty string: an empty delimiter splits the path per character, and the prefix LIKE this adapter emits would also match the path itself
